I've been working this land for 30 years, and I know Quzhou's conditions well — dry winters, hot summers, and we rely on the well because rainfall here is never enough. My 1.1 mu has run wheat-maize rotation my whole adult life. My son works in the city now, so it's mostly me handling things, and at my age I'm not going to change what works.

For **wheat**, I'll plant in mid-October after rotary tilling the maize stubble under. I use the improved Jimai variety — not the newest experiment, something I've grown for years. I apply base fertilizer before planting, then top-dress at jointing. Three irrigations: before winter sets in, at jointing, and at heading. I'll spray once for herbicide early on and once for rust or aphids if I see signs — usually I do. Yield around 450 jin per mu is what I expect.

For **maize**, I direct-seed right after wheat harvest in June — no time to waste and no need to till again. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or whatever the supply station has in that family. I'll apply base fertilizer and chase with urea at the big bell stage. Two irrigations, maybe three if July is dry. One herbicide pass after emergence, one more spray if corn borer shows up. I expect around 550 jin per mu.

With some family income off-farm, I'm not desperate, but this land feeds us and brings in a little cash. I keep inputs at the level I know is safe and profitable.
